title: Incremental delta capture heuristic to reduce prefill recaptures and improve replay correctness
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Our multi-stream decode flow still suffers from frequent full CUDA graph recaptures when small changes occur during prefill or when kernel binding/occupancy shifts between streams. These recaptures increase tail latency and reduce GPU utilization. Root causes include: brittle capture boundaries when kernels change shape, inconsistent kernel selection heuristics across prefill/replay, and KV-cache epoch drift that invalidates assumptions made during capture.

Goal: Introduce an incremental delta-capture mechanism plus occupancy-aware kernel selection so that small, localized changes (e.g., different attention kernel due to sequence length variation or a minor kernel fusion decision) produce a lightweight delta patch that can be applied to an existing graph at replay time rather than forcing a full recapture. This should reduce recapture churn, maintain replay correctness across concurrent streams, and preserve SLOs during transient kernel shifts.

Approach:
1) Kernel fingerprinting: compute a compact fingerprint for each capture segment representing kernel variant, launch configuration, and tail-state dependency. Store fingerprints as part of the graph metadata.
2) Incremental delta capture: when a mismatch is detected between current runtime fingerprints and the stored graph metadata, instead of recapturing the entire graph, capture only the minimal set of kernels whose fingerprints differ and emit a delta graph segment. Delta segments are versioned and can be patched into the base graph via a staged swap at runtime.
3) Occupancy-aware selection: during initial capture, choose kernels using an occupancy-cost model (latency trade-off vs occupancy) that prefers stable kernels across expected sequence length distributions. During replay, prefer compatible kernel variants that can be emulated by delta segments rather than unique one-off kernels.
4) Prefill epoching and checksum: add a lightweight KV-cache epoch and checksum validation that detects drift in prefix/KV state between capture and replay. If drift is within tolerated bounds, apply delta patch; otherwise fall back to safe recapture.
5) Safe swap protocol: implement a two-phase swap for patch application: prepare (capture delta and pin resources), validate (run a deterministic test replay of a single token in isolated context), commit (atomic pointer swap to new graph) with automatic rollback on validation failure.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Adds metadata overhead to saved graphs and small runtime CPU cost for fingerprint checks.
- Complexity in managing delta versions across long-lived graphs; will need bounded retention/GC policy.
- Some kernel changes (e.g., major layout/size changes) will still require full recapture; delta approach targets localized shifts only.

Success metrics:
- Reduce full graph recaptures caused by kernel drift by >= 50% on observed workloads.
- Reduce 99th percentile latency during multi-stream prefill by >= 15% on internal benchmark.
- No regressions in replay correctness; KV-checksum false positives <= 0.5%.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for kernel fingerprinting and delta application added
Benchmark: end-to-end multi-stream decode 99p latency improves by at least 15% on internal dataset A
Graph storage and GC handles delta segments without leaking memory after 24h of churn
Fallbacks exercise full recapture path and rollbacks proved in staging with synthetic preemption scenarios
Documentation: confluence design and runtime telemetry (graph.delta.applied, graph.recapture.reason) are emitted
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Raman: Initial design sketch posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Incremental+Capture+Design. Looking for feedback on the fingerprint shape and costs.

2026-02-18 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype of fingerprinting landed (local branch). Approach uses a 64-bit CRC over kernel ID + launch params + static shape. Preliminary perf shows 0.8% CPU overhead on encode path.
2026-02-25 - Performance: Ran synthetic suite (mixed seq lengths). Observed 42% fewer full recaptures when minor kernel variants were present. Need to validate on production trace.
2026-03-02 - Design review with Runtime SIG: concerns raised about delta GC: suggest limits by delta-count-per-graph and TTL. Also suggested adding a compatibility matrix for kernel substitutes.

2026-03-05 - Engineering note: Implemented two-phase swap prototype. Validation step runs a single-step deterministic token generation; observed one failure case due to KV epoch mismatch—added checksum tolerance heuristics.

2026-03-10 - QA: Staging run with preemption injection (simulated driver preempt) passed 90/100 runs; failures due to race in pinned memory lifetime. Created follow-up ENG-158002 to harden pinned memory lifecycle.

2026-03-12 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2145. Includes kernel fingerprinting, delta capture plumbing, and metric emission (graph.delta.applied, graph.delta.rejected).
Blocking: Need runtime-allocator change to allow delta segment pinning without leaking LRU eviction. Contacting infra team to propose allocator extension.
